note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of prostate cancer management following repeat biopsy and rising PSA.

The patient is a 67-year-old retired truck driver living on a working farm with his partner. He presents for re-evaluation of his prostate cancer, initially diagnosed in 2023. PSA has risen from 3.3 ng/mL in May 2022 to 19.0 ng/mL in February 2025. He has a history of hypercholesterolaemia managed with statins and osteoarthritis. He plays tennis twice weekly and abstains from alcohol. Recent appointments include pain clinic for chronic shoulder pain, orthopaedic follow-up for knee osteoarthritis, and sleep clinic evaluation for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. He prefers morning appointments due to public transport reliance.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, non-tender, and symmetrically enlarged without nodularity, consistent with cT1c staging. General examination reveals an alert, well-nourished male with normal vital signs. Musculoskeletal examination shows mild limitation in shoulder range of motion due to chronic pain.
